findings.evidence: I'm not able to verify the account without those details. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: In one turn the agent asks for verification, repeats the request and ends the contact; the transcript shows no customer reply, so the contact is ended while the customer is still asking for help (cancel or discount), with no any-other-help question and no thanks.

doubts: Cancellation request was never handled; not recorded under PR-6 because the agent did not refuse cancellation as such, the single act is the premature ending. If the customer was simply silent the same turn still fails CL-9 (one check-in, not two).

findings.evidence: Is everything clear, and can I help with anything else about your account?
findings.why: Cancellation was processed and recapped, but the agent only asked CL-6-type questions; it never asked the customer to confirm the recap is correct.

doubts: Borderline: 'Is everything clear' could be read as a confirmation request; I read it as a questions check (CL-6), not CL-7. Also turn 9 offers to check for a lower-priced plan although Basic is already the cheapest; no concrete offer or promise was made, so not recorded.

Transcript stops after the agent's repeated verification request (turn 3): no reply, no close, cancellation never handled. No rule is visibly broken because the agent does not end the contact, but the contact is incomplete.

findings.evidence: Is there anything you'd like me to clarify about the cancellation, or any other help you need?
findings.why: Cancellation recap is given with a CL-6 question only; the agent never asks the customer to confirm the recap is correct.

doubts: Transcript ends on the agent's question with no customer reply and no thanks/goodbye; CL-7 could in theory have come later, and CL-11 is not cited because the agent did not visibly end the contact.
Same as ag-04: transcript stops after the agent's repeated verification request, no close and no visible breach; cancellation never handled.

First payment on Oct 15 is exactly day 10 from Oct 5; treated as within the Early limit. Turn 11 says $60 is due Oct 14, which will not be issued after the cancellation in turn 13; not corrected, but no rule requires it.

Turn 7 asks 'Shall I go ahead and cancel?' and announces the cancellation in the same turn; I accepted the customer's 'Cancel my service' in turn 6 as the prior clear yes (PR-5). CL-6/CL-7 were asked in turn 7, before the escalation in turn 9, and not repeated after it; passed because each was asked. Turn 5 mention of the June 30 notice not treated as arguing (TN-2).

findings.evidence: What's your account PIN or the amount of your last payment? ... I couldn't verify you with the information provided.
findings.why: Right after the customer gave name, address and last payment correctly, the agent re-asks for the same item and says it could not verify her; in turn 9 it again asks for a payment now after she twice said the earliest date is October 15. Scripted lines that ignore what the customer just said.

doubts: Agent refused Oct 15 as outside the window although it is exactly 10 days out for an Early account (ag-07 accepted the same date). I found no rule mapped to wrongly refusing a plan that fits (PP-4 covers confirming a contradicting plan), so it is not recorded; it may deserve a false_resolution view. Balance disclosed in turn 5 after three correct items in turn 4, so VR-1 passed despite the agent's own 'couldn't verify'. Transcript ends without a close.

findings.evidence: What days of the month do you usually get paid, and what's the earliest date you could make a payment?
findings.why: The agent never asks why the account fell behind and the customer never says; the payment plan is proposed in turn 13 with the reason unknown.

doubts: Reason for falling behind never asked, but no plan or retention offer was made, so FL-2 not recorded. Agent twice proposes sending an 80-day account to Recovery (turns 7, 9), which only handles accounts over 90 days; no promise about Recovery's decision was made and no rule clearly covers it.

findings.evidence: I can't verify the account, so I can't discuss or arrange payments for it. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent asks for verification, declares it failed and ends the contact in a single turn with no customer reply shown, while the customer is asking to set up payments; no any-other-help question and no thanks.

doubts: Agent states verification failed, but the transcript shows no customer answer to fail.

findings.evidence: Thank you for understanding. Goodbye.
findings.why: An escalation is an action, so CL-6 and CL-7 apply; the agent never asks whether the customer has questions or needs other help and never asks for confirmation of the recap before closing.

doubts: Strict reading. The customer asked questions unprompted, they were answered, and the customer said she understood; a lenient auditor could pass this.

findings.evidence: I couldn't verify you after two tries, so I can't discuss the account. ... goodbye.
findings.why: The whole verification exchange and the close are in one agent turn with no customer reply in the transcript; the contact is ended while the customer is still asking for help with the past-due balance.

doubts: If the agent's statement of two failed tries is taken as fact, VR-6 would justify stopping; I did not, because the transcript shows no customer answers.

findings.evidence: We've ended this contact. Please contact Tolvane again to verify your account and discuss your options.
findings.why: Agent ends the contact in turn 3 before the customer could answer, then refuses to continue when she supplies correct details; her hardship/late-fee question is never answered.

doubts: Turn 5 also ignores what the customer just said (TN-5) but it is the same act as the ending, recorded once.

findings.evidence: Anything else I can help with about this?
findings.why: Escalation done and recapped with a CL-6 question, but the agent never asks the customer to confirm the recap is correct.

doubts: Transcript ends on the agent's question with no close, so CL-7 could in theory have followed. Turn 3 tells the customer to contact Tolvane directly before he could answer, but the contact continued, so CL-10 not recorded.

findings.evidence: Since I couldn't verify the account during this contact, the account holder will need to contact Tolvane directly for help. Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent declares verification failed before any answer, then closes after the customer gives correct details; the late-fee concern is never explained.

doubts: Turn 5 also ignores the customer's correct details (TN-5); same act as the ending, recorded once.

findings.evidence: The account holder can contact Tolvane directly for help. Goodbye.
findings.why: Customer says he already called last week about the same unresolved drops; a repeat contact must be escalated and no escalation is made.

findings.evidence: I'm sorry, I still can't verify you. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent ends the contact in a single turn with no customer reply shown, while the customer is still asking for help; no any-other-help question and no thanks.

doubts: Both come from the same closing turn. I recorded both because the escalation duty and the closing duties (CL-6, CL-11) are separate obligations; under a tighter one-act reading only one would count.

findings.evidence: The contact is escalated. Thank you for letting me know, and goodbye.
findings.why: Escalation is an action; the agent closes in the same turn without asking about questions or other help and without asking the customer to confirm the recap.

doubts: Strict reading of section 10 (escalation triggers all CL rules). Escalation itself is correct and complete under ES-3/ES-8.

findings.evidence: Sorry, I can't share his balance or due date. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent offers a third-party payment and ends the contact in the same turn without waiting for an answer, without asking if other help is needed and without thanking the customer.

doubts: 'I can't share his balance or due date' echoes the customer's own words; not treated as confirming a balance (VR-3).

findings.evidence: Your payment of $35 was received. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: A payment is an action; the agent asks the amount, announces the payment and closes in one turn with no customer reply, no questions check and no confirmation of the recap.

findings.evidence: What amount would you like to pay? ... Your payment of $35 was received.
findings.why: The third party must choose the amount; the transcript shows no amount from the caller, so the $35 comes from the agent.

doubts: VR-4 finding is uncertain: nothing about the account was disclosed, and if the payment statement is taken to imply the caller named $35 off-transcript, privacy passes.

findings.evidence: Meredith can contact Tolvane directly for help with the plan change.
findings.why: Caller says the account is in his wife's name and asks for a downgrade; a non-holder asking for a change must be escalated, and the agent instead tries to verify him and then sends him away.

findings.evidence: Thanks for contacting Tolvane. Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent closes in a single turn with no customer reply shown and never asks whether he needs any other help.

doubts: Premature closure is the weaker finding; the ending is largely the same act as the missed escalation. 'I still need one more verification detail' not treated as confirming the account (VR-3).

findings.evidence: I'm sorry for your loss. ... Eugene will need to contact Tolvane directly
findings.why: Agent acknowledges the death and in the same turn tells the caller that the deceased account holder must contact Tolvane, a scripted line that ignores what the customer said.

findings.evidence: Your ticket number is TV-44201. Thank you for contacting Tolvane, and goodbye.
findings.why: Escalation is an action; the agent closes without asking about questions or other help and without asking for confirmation of the recap.

doubts: ES-7 applied from turn 2 and the escalation came one turn late (turn 5); not recorded as missed because it was made. TN-5 is a judgement call: the caller had said 'settling affairs', not 'died', in turn 2.

findings.evidence: I'm unable to verify you, so I can't discuss the account. ... Goodbye.
findings.why: Agent asks for verification, declares it failed and ends the contact in one turn with no customer reply shown; no any-other-help question and no thanks.

doubts: Agent states verification failed, but the transcript shows no customer answer to fail.
